items.summary: In a published opinion filed November 12, 2026, the Ninth Circuit affirmed in part and reversed in part the District of Arizona's dismissal of Sabrina Beram's action against the City of Sedona, and remanded. The panel held that Beram alleged an Article III injury and had standing to seek injunctive relief based on the city's credible threat of enforcing its ordinance prohibiting sleeping in a vehicle. The panel further held that Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act may cover a failure to provide reasonable accommodation that would allow a person with a disability to comply with a criminal ordinance, and it affirmed dismissal of the Eighth Amendment claim, which Beram abandoned.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam judgment filed November 12, 2026, the D.C. Circuit affirmed the District of Columbia district court's May 7, 2026 order dismissing Philip Hahn's complaint for lack of jurisdiction. The court held that the United States and Supreme Court staff are immune from damages suits based on official actions of judicial clerks that are an integral part of the judicial process, and that the jurisdictional question is not a factual issue requiring a jury. The Clerk was directed to withhold issuance of the mandate until seven days after resolution of any timely rehearing petition.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam judgment filed November 12, 2026, the D.C. Circuit affirmed the District of Columbia district court's dismissal of Darrell Harper's complaint against the United States and Donald J. Trump, and denied his motion to appoint counsel. The court held that damages claims against the United States were barred by sovereign immunity, and that the administration was not a proper defendant for claims based entirely on the actions of judicial officers. The court also affirmed on the alternative ground that the complaint sought review of orders of the Southern District of Texas, which the district court lacked jurisdiction to review, and noted that the dismissal was without prejudice to filing a new complaint.

items.summary: In an unpublished per curiam opinion dated November 12, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit affirmed the judgment in United States v.   The SPEAKER pro tempore. Pursuant to clause 8 of rule XX, the
unfinished business is the vote on adoption of the resolution (H. Res.
1247) providing for consideration o
items.summary: On a 271-135 vote with 26 not voting (Roll No. 322), the House adopted H. Res. 1247, providing for consideration of H.R. 2102, the Major Richard Star Act. As considered, the bill amends sections 1413a and 1414 of title 10, United States Code, to expand combat-related special compensation eligibility to chapter 61 disability retirees with fewer than 20 years of creditable service and to end the concurrent receipt phase-in provisions, effective the first day of the first month after enactment. The bill was made debatable for one hour, divided among the chairs and ranking members of the Committees on Armed Services and Veterans' Affairs or their designees.
items.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 2102, MAJOR RICHARD STAR ACT

items.summary: Representative Green of Texas delivered a 60-minute special order stating an intention to give notice of a House vote on articles of impeachment against President Donald John Trump as early as the following week. The speech referred to a House vote of 204 members to advance articles of impeachment against Secretary of War Hegseth, a letter the speaker sent to the President, and U.S. military operations in Iran. Schweikert of Arizona was recognized for 60 minutes as the designee of
the majority leader.)
  Mr. SCHWEIKERT. Mr. Speaker, I apprec
items.summary: Representative Schweikert of Arizona delivered a 60-minute special order on federal spending, debt, and demographics, citing a 10-year Treasury yield above 5 percent and a 30-year home loan rate above 7 percent. The speech compared projections of 2026 tax receipts from OMB ($6 trillion), CBO ($5.6 trillion), and the Treasury ($5.4 trillion), and stated that about 24 percent of federal spending is subject to annual congressional votes. The speaker also stated that total net interest is about $1.2 trillion and that the majority of federal spending is projected to go to individuals over age 65 within about 20-some months.
items.title: MATH PROBLEM

items.summary: Representative Roy of Texas delivered a 30-minute address on voter concerns following the 2026 election, citing a national debt of $42 trillion and the need to secure the border. The speech read a paraphrased social media post describing a hypothetical Ohio voter facing higher gas and grocery prices and a son unable to find work, and it referred to concerns about data centers, artificial intelligence, and Republican losses in Texas. The speaker stated that Congress was not consulted before U.S. military action against Iran and that Congress should have been asked to authorize it.

items.summary: Representative Grothman of Wisconsin delivered a 30-minute address on immigration, stating that about one-sixth of the U.S. population is foreign-born and that roughly 800,000 people were naturalized each year before last year. He stated that a bill barring federal welfare benefits to noncitizens was not brought to the floor, and he described federal program provisions that he said penalize married couples with children. He asked the White House, possibly with Vice President Vance, to form a commission to recommend ways to address those program provisions.

items.summary: Senator Bennet submitted amendment SA 6950 to amendment SA 6883 to H.R. 2347, proposing a new Title IV, 'Mining Reform', to be added at the end of division B. The title defines terms including 'casual use,' 'exploration,' 'locatable mineral,' 'mineral activity,' and 'undue degradation,' and it limits the issuance of patents to mining claims for which a patent application was filed by September 30, 1994, with the requirements fully complied with. items.summary: Senators Bennet, Schiff, and Lujan submitted amendment SA 6956 to amendment SA 6883 to H.R. 2347, proposing to replace a section of the bill concerning federal environmental review procedures. The text requires federal agencies to publish draft environmental impact statements and environmental assessments in the Federal Register, with a Tribal consultation period and a public comment period each of not less than 45 days, and it sets deadlines of 1 year for environmental assessments and 2 years for environmental impact statements. items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service 9 CFR Part 11 [Docket No. APHIS-2026-0067] RIN 0579-AE93 Horse Protection AGENCY: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, USDA. ACTION: Proposed rule. SUMMARY: On May
items.summary: On May 8, 2024, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) of the United States Department of Agriculture published in the Federal Register a final rule that amended the regulations promulgated under the Horse Protection Act (the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule). APHIS is proposing to remove the provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule that have been vacated by court order and proposing to withdraw the remaining non-vacated provisions of the May 2024 Horse Protection final rule to ensure that the regulations afford due process and better align with the Act. APHIS is also proposing to amend the regulations by revising, among other things, the certification requirements for training and licensing of designated qualified persons (DQPs); enhancing DQP inspection procedures and the process for appealing APHIS inspections before any possible disqualification by management; and clarifying that if a horse is determined to be sore, it is disqualified from participating in the class in which the inspection took place and not the entire event.
items.title: Horse Protection

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 180 [EPA-HQ-OPP-2026-5678; FRL-13569-01] Isocycloseram; Pesticide Tolerance for Emergency Exemption AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). ACTION: Final rule. SUMMARY: This regulation esta
items.summary: This regulation establishes a time-limited tolerance for residues of isocycloseram, including its metabolites and degradates, in or on sunflowers. This action is in response to EPA's authorization of a specific exemption under the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) authorizing use of the pesticide on sunflowers. This regulation establishes a maximum permissible level for residues of isocycloseram in or on sunflower, seed at 0.4 parts per million. The time-limited tolerance expires on December 31, 2029.
items.title: Isocycloseram; Pesticide Tolerance for Emergency Exemption

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13813; Project Identifier AD-2026-00061-E] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines AGENCY: Federal Aviation Ad
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model GE Passport 20-17BB1A, GE Passport 20-18BB1A, GE Passport 20-19BB1A, and GE Passport 20-19BB1B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) due to an engine fire caused by fuel leakage within the engine core compartment. This proposed AD would require replacement of a certain start bleed valve (SBV) fuel tube with a redesigned SBV fuel tube. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. (P&WC) Model PW814GA and PW815GA engines. This proposed AD was prompted by the manufacturer revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the existing airworthiness limitations manual (ALM) to introduce new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. This proposed AD would require updating the ALS of the existing ALM or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive instructions and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney Canada Corp. Engines

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 52 [EPA-R10-OAR-2026-2972; FRL-13338-01-R10] Air Plan Approval; Oregon Department of Environmental Quality; Emission Standards and Controls for Sources Emitting Gasoline Vapors AGENCY: Environment
items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve a revision to the Oregon State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) on December 17, 2025, for the Portland and Salem/Keizer, Oregon 1979 1-hour ozone maintenance areas. The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The proposed revisions also include more widespread adoption of Stage I Enhanced Vapor Recovery, Stage I vapor balance, and enhanced conventional nozzles, among other changes. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Oregon Department of Environmental Quality; Emission Standards and Controls for Sources Emitting Gasoline Vapors

items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 747-400 and 747-400F series airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of an overheated alternating current motor pump (ACMP) that caused a fire in the main landing gear (MLG) wheel well. This proposed AD would require a maintenance records check or inspection for any installed ACMP with a certain part number and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.opening_verbatim: DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Federal Aviation Administration 14 CFR Part 39 [Docket No. FAA-2026-13802; Project Identifier AD-2026-00597-T] RIN 2120-AA64 Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes AGENCY: Federal Aviation Admini
items.summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that certain wing skin outer mold line (OML) penetrating fasteners installed using threaded nuts without cap seals do not provide reliable protection against potential ignition sources when subjected to direct attachment lightning currents. This proposed AD would require inspecting between certain ribs on the left and right wing for wing skin penetrating fasteners with a threaded nut adjacent to the electromagnetic effects (EME) sleeve; inspecting the left and right wing fuel tanks, surge tanks, and dry bays for threaded nuts installed on fasteners that penetrate the upper and lower wing skins; accomplishing the inspection specified in a certain airworthiness limitation (AWL); and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also require accomplishing concurrent requirements and revising the maintenance program to incorporate the airworthiness limitation task. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
items.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

items.summary: Presidential Determination No. 2027-02, dated October 28, 2026, is a memorandum to the Secretaries of State, the Treasury, and Energy. It determines under section 1245(d)(4)(B) and (C) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (Public Law 112-81) that there is a sufficient supply of petroleum and petroleum products from countries other than Iran to permit a significant reduction in the volume purchased from Iran by or through foreign financial institutions. The document directs the Secretary of State to publish the determination in the Federal Register, and it was filed on November 12, 2026.

items.opening_verbatim: IB One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 4930 AN ACT To expand the sharing of
items.summary: H.R. 4930 (enrolled, 119th Congress, Second Session) amends Section 628A of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) to expand information sharing on suspected intellectual property rights violations in trade. The amendments change the standard from "suspects" to "has a reasonable suspicion," extend covered items to packaging, packing materials, containers, and labels, and authorize U.S. Customs and Border Protection to provide nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces, express consignment operators, freight forwarders, and other entities involved in importation, with notice to the person as prescribed by the Secretary. The Act also adds "any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner" to the parties eligible under subsection (b).
items.title: HR 4930 ENR: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.

items.opening_verbatim: I One Hundred Nineteenth Congress of the United States of America At the Second Session Begun and held at the City of Washington on Saturday, the third day of January, two thousand and twenty-six H. R. 8552 AN ACT To increase, effective as
items.summary: H.R. 8552 (enrolled, 119th Congress, Second Session), titled "Veterans’ Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026," directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to increase, effective December 1, 2026, the dollar amounts for disability compensation and dependency and indemnity compensation under specified provisions of title 38, United States Code, including sections 1114, 1115(1), 1162, 1311(a) through (d), 1313(a), and 1314. Each amount is increased by the same percentage as the Social Security benefit increase effective December 1, 2026, under section 215(i) of the Social Security Act, and the Secretary may administratively adjust certain rates under section 10 of Public Law 85-857. The Secretary must publish the adjusted amounts in the Federal Register by the date required under section 215(i)(2)(D) of the Social Security Act for a determination made during fiscal year 2027.

items.summary: H.R. 3978, the Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act, passed the House of Representatives on November 9, 2026, and was received in the Senate and placed on the Senate calendar as Calendar No. 695 on November 10, 2026. The bill amends section 11 v. of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2014(v)) to add reprocessing to the list of activities in the definition of production facility, and to provide that the definition does not include reprocessing spent nuclear fuel in a manner that does not isolate plutonium. items.summary: S. 1759, the Supersonic Aviation Modernization Act, was introduced by Senator Budd and cosponsors on May 14, 2025, and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. The committee reported the bill with an amendment on November 10, 2026, as Report No. 119-160 and Calendar No. 694. As reported, the bill directs the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration to issue a final rule within 2 years of enactment that creates a noise-based certification standard for civil supersonic aircraft, after consulting with the Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, with takeoff and landing noise levels not exceeding those required for subsonic aircraft in operation as of enactment, and with a process for periodic review and updating of the standards.
